generation.hypothesis: SPS near 1000 °C will transform metastable BCC MgAlTiVFeCo powder into a dense microstructure containing uniformly distributed oxide barrier phases, thereby maximizing hardness and retaining corrosion and oxidation resistance despite the alloy’s tendency to form intermetallic compounds.
generation.material_initial_state: The starting material will be ball-milled MgAlTiVFeCo powder containing a simple, non-equilibrium BCC solid solution.
generation.intervention: The powder will be consolidated by spark plasma sintering, with 1000 °C compared against otherwise matched medium-to-low sintering temperatures.
generation.conditions: SPS temperatures will span 800–1000 °C. Oxidation will be tested in air at 900 °C, and corrosion will be tested in 3.5 wt% NaCl.
generation.structural_mediator: Near 1000 °C, a dense microstructure with uniformly distributed AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3 barrier phases will be expected.
generation.mechanism: High temperature and pressure will increase diffusion sufficiently to promote densification and a dense, continuous passive film with high polarization resistance. This film should impede chloride penetration and favor local penetration-defense behavior. Oxidation should remain diffusion-controlled, following parabolic kinetics with two growth regimes.
generation.predicted_outcome: The 1000 °C condition should reach about 97% relative density and 1200–1250 HV, with oxidation constants near 0.04 and 0.1 mg^2·cm^-4·s^-1 across the two regimes. Corrosion potential should shift positively to roughly -0.44 V and current density should fall to about 1×10^-6 A·cm^-2.
generation.baseline: Samples sintered at 850–950 °C should have lower density, hardness, and corrosion and oxidation resistance because their barrier phases will be less effective.
generation.boundary: Below 800 °C, insufficient sintering force should limit density to around 80% or less; above 1000 °C, magnesium volatilization could prevent retention of the proposed benefits.
generation.uncertainty: Competing decomposition of the metastable solid solution into intermetallic compounds may alter the transformation pathway or its kinetics.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare matched MgAlTiVFeCo powders SPS-consolidated at 1000 °C and lower temperatures, then expose them to the specified oxidation and corrosion environments.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be falsified if the 1000 °C sample lacks parabolic biphasic oxidation kinetics or fails to show a more positive corrosion potential and lower current density than the lower-temperature controls.
